transcript.text: induction hob keeps turnin off after 5-10 mins on high, have to keep restartin it. drives me nuts. any1 know y?

That usually happens because the hob's safety system detects overheating. The most common cause is blocked ventilation under or around the unit, or using pans that don't transfer heat efficiently (which makes the sensor think it's too hot). Please check that the vents aren't obstructed and that you're using flat-based induction pans. If those are fine, does an error code appear on the display when it cuts out?
sometimes a small code flashes but i didnt catch it. pans are induction ones. fan roars before it cuts out tho. new drawer unit went in under it a month ago, started after that

The roaring fan is a key clue: it suggests the hob's safety system has detected high heat and forced the fans to run at maximum speed before cutting power. Given that this started after you installed new drawers underneath, there is a very strong chance they are blocking the ventilation slots that let cool air in or hot air out. Please switch off and isolate the power first (unplug it if possible, or turn off the fused spur). Then check underneath and around the edges of the hob for any gaps that might have been covered by the new drawers. If you can see a sticker with the make and model number under the glass, please tell me what it says so I can confirm exactly where the vents are located.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
not pulling the drawers out or looking under the hob, dont know the model either. is there anything else i can try?

Since you can't look under the hob or find the model number right now, let's try a quick test to confirm if the airflow is the issue. Turn off all zones and let the hob cool down completely. Then switch just one zone on high for about 1 minute. If the fan roars loudly again before it cuts out, that suggests the safety system is detecting heat buildup—most likely because the new drawers are blocking the air intake or exhaust. If the fan sounds normal but it still cuts out after a few minutes, the cooling fan itself may have failed and will need an engineer to replace.
ok did that. fan roars then it cuts out after a few mins on the big front one. works again after it cools down a few mins. so whats the fix?

[Heading: Likely cause: pan misuse / blocked vents / airflow]
The fix depends on what is blocking the airflow. Since this started after you installed new drawers and the fan roars loudly before cutting out, the most likely cause is that the drawers are obstructing the hob's air intake or exhaust vents. Even if they look clear from the outside, internal ducts might be blocked by cabinet material or debris. If you can safely check underneath without pulling the drawers out fully (e.g., looking through gaps), try to ensure there is at least a few centimetres of space around the hob's ventilation slots. If you cannot access that area, or if clearing it doesn't help, the fan itself may have failed and will need an engineer to replace.
